MODEL OUTPUT

———

Feature sensitivity

Each feature is replaced with its training median, with all others held fixed. The change in score is a sensitivity check, not a causal explanation or SHAP attribution.

Unusual combinations may be outside the training distribution. A calibrated score is an estimate, not a guarantee.

EXPERIMENT DESIGN

Evaluate decisions, not accuracy

Use earlier transactions to learn a ranking, calibrate the scores on a later period, and choose a model and cutoff on validation. Evaluate the locked decision on a final untouched time period.

Why these models?

Logistic regression is a fast, interpretable baseline. Gradient boosting can capture nonlinear feature interactions. Both use balanced training weights; a separate unweighted sigmoid calibrator adjusts scores to the calibration period’s observed prevalence.

Selection rule

The original 1% policy was locked before test evaluation. The controls are for subsequent exploration and do not replace the precommitted result.

MEASURED HELD-OUT RESULTS

Baseline vs. boosting

AP = average precision, a ranking metric useful with rare fraud. ROC AUC is also reported, but is not the selection criterion. Brier measures score error; lower is better. Recall intervals are 1,000 bootstrap resamples of test fraud cases at the original cutoff.

LIMITATIONS & NEXT EXPERIMENT

What this result can support

Data provenance

Deployment boundary

The browser runs real exported estimators, with Python/JavaScript parity checks. This is an offline prototype with retrospective labels; it has no payment integration, label-delay handling, or production monitoring.

Business assumptions

Costs and the fraction of fraud prevented are assumptions. The dataset cannot measure actual customer attrition, chargeback outcomes, or the effect of intervention.

Next validation

Rerun on real transactions, add multiple rolling time windows, examine subgroup calibration, and run shadow scoring before proposing an experiment. Measure reviewer yield and customer friction with delayed fraud labels.
